### Basic Candlestick

These examples use daily Apple stock prices from February 2015 to February 2017.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv")
df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date)
df <- tail(df, 30)

fig <- df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_candlestick(
    x = ~Date,
    open = ~AAPL.Open,
    close = ~AAPL.Close,
    high = ~AAPL.High,
    low = ~AAPL.Low
  ) |>
  update_layout(title = "Basic Candlestick Chart")

fig
```

### Candlestick without Rangeslider

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv")
df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date)
df <- tail(df, 30)

fig <- df |>
  go_figure() |>

    open = ~AAPL.Open,
    close = ~AAPL.Close,
    high = ~AAPL.High,
    low = ~AAPL.Low

  update_layout(
    title = "Basic Candlestick Chart",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(rangeslider = go_xaxis_rangeslider(visible = FALSE))

fig
```

### Customise the fig ure with Shapes and Annotations

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv")
df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date)

# annotation
a <- go_annotation(
  text = "Brexit vote",
  x = "2016-06-23",
  y = 1.02,
  xref = "x",
  yref = "paper",
  xanchor = "left",
  showarrow = FALSE
)

# use shapes to create a line
l <- go_shape(
  type = "line",
  x0 = "2016-06-23",
  x1 = "2016-06-23",
  y0 = 0,
  y1 = 1,
  xref = "x",
  yref = "paper",
  line = go_shape_line(color = "black", width = 0.5)
)

fig <- df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_candlestick(
    x = ~Date,
    open = ~AAPL.Open,
    close = ~AAPL.Close,
    high = ~AAPL.High,
    low = ~AAPL.Low
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Apple Stock",
    annotations = list(a),
    shapes = list(l)
  )

fig
```

### Custom Candlestick Colors

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv")
df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date)
df <- tail(df, 30)

# custom colors
i <- go_candlestick_increasing(line = go_candlestick_increasing_line(color = "#FFD700"))
d <- go_candlestick_decreasing(line = go_candlestick_decreasing_line(color = "#0000ff"))

fig <- df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_candlestick(
    x = ~Date,
    open = ~AAPL.Open,
    close = ~AAPL.Close,
    high = ~AAPL.High,
    low = ~AAPL.Low,
    increasing = i,
    decreasing = d
  )

fig
```

### Add a Trace to Candlestick Chart

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv")
df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date)
df <- tail(df, 365)

fig <- df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_candlestick(
    x = ~Date,
    open = ~AAPL.Open,
    close = ~AAPL.Close,
    high = ~AAPL.High,
    low = ~AAPL.Low
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~AAPL.Open,
    mode = "lines",
    line = go_scatter_line(color = "black", width = 0.75)
  ) |>
  update_layout(showlegend = FALSE)

fig
```

### Candlestick Using Segments

Each segment is a line between two points, and `NA`s between segments break the line.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

dat <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv")
names(dat) <- sub("^AAPL\\.", "", names(dat))
dat <- subset(dat, Date >= "2016-01-01")

# x and y of the segments from y0 to y1, one per row, separated by NAs
segments <- function(d, y0, y1) {
  list(
    x = as.vector(rbind(d$Date, d$Date, NA)),
    y = as.vector(rbind(d[[y0]], d[[y1]], NA))
  )
}

directions <- c(Decreasing = "red", Increasing = "forestgreen")

fig <- go_figure()
for (dir in names(directions)) {
  d <- dat[dat$direction == dir, ]
  low_high <- segments(d, "Low", "High")
  open_close <- segments(d, "Open", "Close")
  fig <- fig |>
    add_scatter(
      x = low_high$x,
      y = low_high$y,
      mode = "lines",
      line = go_scatter_line(color = directions[[dir]], width = 1),
      hoverinfo = "none"
    ) |>
    add_scatter(
      x = open_close$x,
      y = open_close$y,
      mode = "lines",
      line = go_scatter_line(color = directions[[dir]], width = 3),
      hoverinfo = "none"
    )
}
fig <- fig |>
  update_layout(showlegend = FALSE, yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Price")) |>
  update_xaxes(rangeslider = go_xaxis_rangeslider(visible = TRUE))

fig
```

### Add Bollinger Bands and Buttons

The data set already holds the Bollinger bands (`dn`, `mavg`, `up`) and the
direction of each day.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv")
df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date)

band_line <- go_scatter_line(color = "#ccc", width = 0.5)
direction_colors <- c(Increasing = "#17BECF", Decreasing = "#7F7F7F")

i <- go_candlestick_increasing(line = go_candlestick_increasing_line(color = "#17BECF"))
d <- go_candlestick_decreasing(line = go_candlestick_decreasing_line(color = "#7F7F7F"))

# subplot with shared x axis
fig <- make_subplots(
  rows = 2,
  cols = 1,
  shared_xaxes = TRUE,
  row_heights = c(0.7, 0.2)
)

# plot candlestick chart
fig <- fig |>
  add_candlestick(
    data = df,
    x = ~Date,
    open = ~AAPL.Open,
    close = ~AAPL.Close,
    high = ~AAPL.High,
    low = ~AAPL.Low,
    name = "AAPL",
    increasing = i,
    decreasing = d,
    row = 1,
    col = 1
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    data = df,
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~up,
    name = "B Bands",
    mode = "lines",
    line = band_line,
    legendgroup = "Bollinger Bands",
    hoverinfo = "none",
    row = 1,
    col = 1
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    data = df,
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~dn,
    name = "B Bands",
    mode = "lines",
    line = band_line,
    legendgroup = "Bollinger Bands",
    showlegend = FALSE,
    hoverinfo = "none",
    row = 1,
    col = 1
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    data = df,
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~mavg,
    name = "Mv Avg",
    mode = "lines",
    line = go_scatter_line(color = "#E377C2", width = 0.5),
    hoverinfo = "none",
    row = 1,
    col = 1
  )

# plot volume bar chart
for (dir in names(direction_colors)) {
  fig <- fig |>
    add_bar(
      data = df[df$direction == dir, ],
      x = ~Date,
      y = ~AAPL.Volume,
      name = dir,
      marker = go_bar_marker(color = direction_colors[[dir]]),
      row = 2,
      col = 1
    )
}

# create rangeselector buttons
rs <- go_xaxis_rangeselector(
  visible = TRUE,
  x = 0.5,
  y = -0.055,
  xanchor = "center",
  font = go_font(size = 9),
  buttons = list(
    go_xaxis_rangeselector_button(count = 1, label = "RESET", step = "all"),
    go_xaxis_rangeselector_button(
      count = 1,
      label = "1 YR",
      step = "year",
      stepmode = "backward"
    ),
    go_xaxis_rangeselector_button(
      count = 3,
      label = "3 MO",
      step = "month",
      stepmode = "backward"
    ),
    go_xaxis_rangeselector_button(
      count = 1,
      label = "1 MO",
      step = "month",
      stepmode = "backward"
    )
  )
)

fig <- fig |>
  update_yaxes(title = "Price", row = 1, col = 1) |>
  update_yaxes(title = "Volume", row = 2, col = 1) |>
  update_xaxes(
    rangeselector = rs,
    rangeslider = go_xaxis_rangeslider(visible = FALSE),
    row = 1,
    col = 1
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Apple: 2015-02-17 - 2017-02-16",
    legend = go_legend(
      orientation = "h",
      x = 0.5,
      y = 1,
      xanchor = "center",
      yref = "paper",
      font = go_font(size = 10),
      bgcolor = "transparent"
    )
  )

fig
```

See `go_candlestick()` for more information and chart attribute options!
